In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our method achieves the state-of-the-art performance in both self-supervised learning and fully supervised learning on ImageNet, which is the most convincing evidence of its superiority over the previous methods.

the proposed method can achieve a similar performance to fully supervised ResNet on the ImageNet dataset with a single-layer ResNet classifier, which is trained with a single-stage training process without any extra supervision.

the proposed method is able to achieve a performance comparable to that of the fully supervised learning with only the self-supervised training, and the stronger data augmentations are still able to benefit the contrastive learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method is the first one that could reach the supervised learning upper bound in terms of top-1 image classification accuracy on the ImageNet dataset.
we can use stronger data augmentations for contrastive learning without worrying about overfitting the distorted images to their original ones.
stronger augmentations are not always harmful to contrastive learning and the proposed method is able to fully leverage their benefits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use stronger augmentations to learn better representations by leveraging the distribution divergence between weakly and strongly transformed data.

the distribution of weakly augmented images can be leveraged as an auxiliary signal to guide the learning of strongly augmented queries to be distinguishable from the negative samples, and this is crucial for pushing the performance of self-supervised learning to the upper bound of supervised learning.

the stronger augmentations can be effectively used in contrastive learning by minimizing the distribution divergence between weakly and strongly transformed samples, which can be further used to push the unsupervised representation learning to the supervised upper bound.
